regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia with acute illness
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Admit and initiate emergency induction under the GTN specialist. Reassess after each two-day block and document the intended transition to EMA/CO or EMA/EP. Serial validated hCG tracks disease response.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia with acute illness
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Etoposide · Stops dividing cells repairing breaks in their DNA. Cisplatin · Joins strands of DNA together so dividing cancer cells cannot copy their DNA normally.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Both medicines on days 1 and 2. The specialist may repeat the block weekly for 1–3 weeks. The GTN team decides when to switch to EMA/CO or EMA/EP, combinations of chemotherapy medicines used after induction.
key_points: Emergency induction for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) with acute illness from liver or central nervous system involvement. Large lung metastases can put breathing at particular risk.

Admit and initiate emergency induction under the GTN specialist. Reassess after each two-day block and document the intended transition to EMA/CO or EMA/EP. Serial validated hCG tracks disease response.
The GTN team decides when to switch to EMA/CO or EMA/EP, combinations of chemotherapy medicines used after induction.
In a specialist-centre cohort, early deaths occurred in 1 of 140 patients in the later treatment era and 11 of 151 in the earlier era. Only 33 of the 140 received induction EP.
regimen_profiles.review_status: Feasibility build. Independent clinical, pharmacy and patient review pending.

patient_selection.treatment_intent: This short first treatment aims to bring the disease under control while your hospital team stabilises you and prepares the next treatment.
patient_selection.disease_and_biomarker_context: Emergency induction for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) with acute illness from liver or central nervous system involvement. Large lung metastases can put breathing at particular risk.
eligibility_orientation: Admit and initiate emergency induction under the GTN specialist. Reassess after each two-day block and document the intended transition to EMA/CO or EMA/EP. Serial validated hCG tracks disease response.
important_cautions: Tell ward staff immediately about new breathlessness, coughing blood, a severe headache, confusion or a seizure. At home, call 112 or 999 for severe breathing difficulty, collapse or a seizure. Call the oncology number urgently for fever or shaking chills.

administration.schedule: Both medicines on days 1 and 2. The specialist may repeat the block weekly for 1–3 weeks.
administration.route_and_duration: Treatment starts urgently in hospital. On each treatment day etoposide runs into a vein over about one hour, followed by cisplatin over about two hours. Extra fluid before cisplatin helps protect the kidneys.
practical_workflow: Your team monitors your breathing, blood pressure and fluid balance during both infusions.
Both medicines are given again. Bring the anti-sickness record from yesterday so the team can check the doses already given.
The GTN team decides when to switch to EMA/CO or EMA/EP, combinations of chemotherapy medicines used after induction.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: High emetogenic risk on both infusion medicines combined, driven by cisplatin; reconcile the single dated multiday course at each visit.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: One dated course for days 1–4. Continue on return visits. Confirm rescue medication, dose and duration before signing.
Reconcile anti-sickness and steroid doses given in hospital with home doses. Review sedation and prescribe breakthrough treatment individually.
patient_education: Tell the nurse at once if you feel faint, hot or breathless during the infusion.
Report ringing ears, trouble hearing, tingling, reduced urine or vomiting that prevents drinking.
Kidney-protecting fluid is given before cisplatin. Follow your dated anti-sickness plan and call if vomiting prevents drinking.
Keep your 24-hour oncology number and treatment card with you. Report fever or sudden illness straight away, including at night and during a break.

baseline: Blood count, kidney and liver tests and a blood pregnancy-hormone test (hCG) help the team assess illness and plan treatment.
before_each_cycle: Blood counts and kidney and liver tests are repeated. The team checks hCG on day 1 of each cycle and more often if needed.
The NCCP schedule checks hCG every two weeks for six months, monthly for six months, then every two months for two years.
priority_toxicities: Infusion reaction or low blood pressure
urgent_review_signals: Tell ward staff immediately about new breathlessness, coughing blood, a severe headache, confusion or a seizure. At home, call 112 or 999 for severe breathing difficulty, collapse or a seizure. Call the oncology number urgently for fever or shaking chills.

longitudinal_schedule.title: Tests and timing

rows.label: At admission
cells: Blood count, kidney and liver tests and a blood pregnancy-hormone test (hCG) help the team assess illness and plan treatment.
Tell the team about ringing in the ears, hearing loss or tingling. Hearing tests and a measured kidney clearance may be needed.

rows.label: During induction
cells: Blood counts and kidney and liver tests are repeated. The team checks hCG on day 1 of each cycle and more often if needed.
If a third block is planned, ask about the 24-hour urine collection used to measure kidney clearance beforehand.

rows.label: After remission and consolidation
cells: The NCCP schedule checks hCG every two weeks for six months, monthly for six months, then every two months for two years.
Get your own testing dates and specialist contact details before leaving hospital.

longitudinal_schedule.note: Your team records the dates and arranges extra tests if your symptoms or results change.

treatment_rationale.summary: In a specialist-centre cohort, early deaths occurred in 1 of 140 patients in the later treatment era and 11 of 151 in the earlier era. Only 33 of the 140 received induction EP.
treatment_rationale.setting: Gestational trophoblastic neoplasia with acute illness
treatment_rationale.limitations: This was a historical comparison of treatment eras. Selection for induction and changes in care prevent attribution of the mortality difference to EP alone.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Confirm IGCCCG prognostic group, histology, tumour-marker profile and the rationale for a bleomycin-free curative regimen. Gynaecology is a catalogue cross-listing. The PDF gives C62 for 00301a and does not establish a separate ovarian indication. The consultant approves any treatment delay.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Etoposide · Stops dividing cells repairing breaks in their DNA. Cisplatin · Joins strands of DNA together so dividing cancer cells cannot copy their DNA normally.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Both medicines on days 1–5 of a 21-day cycle. Four cycles are planned if treatment remains suitable. Days 6–21 have no scheduled EP infusions. Your blood count can still fall. The next cycle starts only after review.
key_points: NCCP 00301a covers good-prognosis metastatic seminoma and non-seminoma by International Germ Cell Cancer Collaborative Group criteria. The published indication carries ICD-10 C62 (testis).

Days 6–21 have no scheduled EP infusions. Your blood count can still fall. The next cycle starts only after review.
Among 944 patients treated with four cycles of EP at one centre, estimated five-year progression-free survival was 93.9% and overall survival was 97.9%.

patient_selection.treatment_intent: The aim is to cure a germ-cell tumour that has spread. Each course includes five days of chemotherapy followed by time for recovery.
patient_selection.disease_and_biomarker_context: NCCP 00301a covers good-prognosis metastatic seminoma and non-seminoma by International Germ Cell Cancer Collaborative Group criteria. The published indication carries ICD-10 C62 (testis).
eligibility_orientation: Confirm IGCCCG prognostic group, histology, tumour-marker profile and the rationale for a bleomycin-free curative regimen. Gynaecology is a catalogue cross-listing. The PDF gives C62 for 00301a and does not establish a separate ovarian indication. The consultant approves any treatment delay.
important_cautions: Call your oncology unit urgently for fever, shaking chills, unexpected bleeding or sudden illness, including during the treatment break. Sudden chest pain, collapse or severe breathlessness needs emergency help.

administration.schedule: Both medicines on days 1–5 of a 21-day cycle. Four cycles are planned if treatment remains suitable.
administration.route_and_duration: Each treatment day starts with etoposide into a vein over about one hour. You also receive fluid before cisplatin, which runs over about one hour. Allow extra time for blood tests, hydration and review.
practical_workflow: Bring your medicines list. The team checks your treatment plan and dates one anti-sickness course for the whole block.
On each of these four days both infusions and kidney-protecting fluid are repeated. Show the team your dated anti-sickness plan each day.
Days 6–21 have no scheduled EP infusions. Your blood count can still fall. The next cycle starts only after review.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: High emetogenic risk on both infusion medicines combined, driven by cisplatin; reconcile the single dated multiday course at each visit.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: One dated course for days 1–7. Continue on return visits. Confirm rescue medication, dose and duration before signing.
Reconcile anti-sickness and steroid doses given in hospital with home doses. Review sedation and prescribe breakthrough treatment individually.
patient_education: Tell the nurse at once if you feel faint, hot or breathless during the infusion.
Report ringing ears, trouble hearing, tingling, reduced urine or vomiting that prevents drinking.
Kidney-protecting fluid is given before cisplatin. Follow your dated anti-sickness plan and call if vomiting prevents drinking.
Keep your 24-hour oncology number and treatment card with you. Report fever or sudden illness straight away, including at night and during a break.

baseline: Blood count, kidney and liver function are checked. The team considers a hearing test and discusses fertility preservation, including sperm banking where appropriate.
before_each_cycle: A blood count is checked weekly. Kidney and liver tests are repeated before each cycle. A change in hearing may prompt audiology.
Your specialist plans scans and tumour-marker tests according to your disease. AFP, beta-hCG and LDH may be relevant depending on tumour type and earlier results.
priority_toxicities: Infusion reaction or low blood pressure
urgent_review_signals: Call your oncology unit urgently for fever, shaking chills, unexpected bleeding or sudden illness, including during the treatment break. Sudden chest pain, collapse or severe breathlessness needs emergency help.

longitudinal_schedule.title: Tests and timing

rows.label: Before the first cycle
cells: Blood count, kidney and liver function are checked. The team considers a hearing test and discusses fertility preservation, including sperm banking where appropriate.
Raise fertility questions before the first infusion, even if you are unsure about future plans.

rows.label: During each cycle
cells: A blood count is checked weekly. Kidney and liver tests are repeated before each cycle. A change in hearing may prompt audiology.
Keep your weekly blood appointment during the break. Report numbness, ringing in the ears, or a change in how much urine you pass.

rows.label: At response review
cells: Your specialist plans scans and tumour-marker tests according to your disease. AFP, beta-hCG and LDH may be relevant depending on tumour type and earlier results.
Ask which markers matter for you and how any residual mass will be assessed.

longitudinal_schedule.note: Your team records the dates and arranges extra tests if your symptoms or results change.

treatment_rationale.summary: Among 944 patients treated with four cycles of EP at one centre, estimated five-year progression-free survival was 93.9% and overall survival was 97.9%.
treatment_rationale.limitations: This observational evidence is principally from testicular germ-cell disease. It does not provide a separate ovarian-specific outcome estimate.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: First-line maintenance after a platinum response
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Confirm complete or partial response after first-line platinum, stage III/IV high-grade epithelial disease, ECOG 0–1 and marrow and organ recovery. Record the last platinum date and discuss alternatives, tumour BRCA/HRD results, monitoring and patient preferences. NCCP 00904 does not require a BRCA mutation.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: First-line maintenance after a platinum response
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Rucaparib · Blocks enzymes called PARP that help repair DNA. Some ovarian cancer cells depend on these repairs to survive.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Take the prescribed dose twice daily, about 12 hours apart, every day. There is no planned week off. Start within eight weeks of the final platinum dose. Treatment lasts up to two years and may stop earlier if the cancer grows or side effects make continued treatment unsuitable.
key_points: First-line maintenance for adults whose stage III or IV high-grade epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer has responded completely or partially to platinum chemotherapy.

Confirm complete or partial response after first-line platinum, stage III/IV high-grade epithelial disease, ECOG 0–1 and marrow and organ recovery. Record the last platinum date and discuss alternatives, tumour BRCA/HRD results, monitoring and patient preferences. NCCP 00904 does not require a BRCA mutation.
Start within eight weeks of the final platinum dose. Treatment lasts up to two years and may stop earlier if the cancer grows or side effects make continued treatment unsuitable.

In the randomised ATHENA-MONO update, median progression-free survival was 20.2 months with rucaparib and 9.2 months with placebo in the overall trial population (hazard ratio 0.53, 95% CI 0.42–0.69).

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Chemotherapy has reduced the cancer. These tablets aim to keep it under control for longer. Your team will explain how your response and tumour test results inform your options.
patient_selection.disease_and_biomarker_context: First-line maintenance for adults whose stage III or IV high-grade epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer has responded completely or partially to platinum chemotherapy.
eligibility_orientation: Confirm complete or partial response after first-line platinum, stage III/IV high-grade epithelial disease, ECOG 0–1 and marrow and organ recovery. Record the last platinum date and discuss alternatives, tumour BRCA/HRD results, monitoring and patient preferences. NCCP 00904 does not require a BRCA mutation.
important_cautions: Call the oncology unit urgently for fever, shaking chills, unexpected bleeding, worsening breathlessness or vomiting that prevents drinking. Report unusual bruising or persistent fatigue promptly.

administration.schedule: Take the prescribed dose twice daily, about 12 hours apart, every day. There is no planned week off.
administration.route_and_duration: Swallow the prescribed tablets whole with a large glass of water, with or without food. Leave a missed or vomited dose out and take only your next scheduled dose. Never crush the tablets or take extra to catch up.
practical_workflow: Check the strength and number of tablets against the latest dispensing label. A dose reduction can change both. Mark morning and evening doses separately.
Start within eight weeks of the final platinum dose. Treatment lasts up to two years and may stop earlier if the cancer grows or side effects make continued treatment unsuitable.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Moderate-to-high oral risk; NCCP allows moderate classification based on clinical experience. Individualise the oral anti-sickness plan.
premedication_and_prophylaxis: One daily anti-sickness dose where prescribed. Record the stop or review date separately from the twice-daily rucaparib schedule.
Choose one oral 5-HT3 antagonist if indicated by the local plan. Review constipation, QT risk, liver function and interacting medicines.
patient_education: Call about persistent fatigue, breathlessness, infections or unusual bruising. Regular blood tests can detect problems before you feel unwell.
Use the morning and evening tablet plan. Ask about any new medicine, including over-the-counter medicines, before starting it. Protect exposed skin from sunlight.
Rucaparib can cause nausea. Your team may prescribe a daily anti-sickness tablet and separate rescue treatment. Ask which one to take and when.
Use effective contraception during treatment and for six months after the last dose if you could become pregnant. Avoid breastfeeding during treatment and for two weeks afterwards.

baseline: The team checks your blood count, kidney and liver function and pregnancy status where relevant.
before_each_cycle: A full blood count checks for anaemia, infection risk and bruising. Kidney and liver blood tests help detect side effects you may not feel.
Persistent low blood counts need closer monitoring and can require haematology review. Your team sets the timing of tests before restarting.
priority_toxicities: Nausea, changes in taste or bowel habit
urgent_review_signals: Call the oncology unit urgently for fever, shaking chills, unexpected bleeding, worsening breathlessness or vomiting that prevents drinking. Report unusual bruising or persistent fatigue promptly.

longitudinal_schedule.title: Tests and timing

rows.label: Before starting
cells: The team checks your blood count, kidney and liver function and pregnancy status where relevant.
Confirm your last platinum date and ask your pharmacist to check prescribed medicines, painkillers, supplements and herbal products.

rows.label: Each month
cells: A full blood count checks for anaemia, infection risk and bruising. Kidney and liver blood tests help detect side effects you may not feel.
Keep the appointment even when you feel well. If a result changes, extra blood tests or a pause may be needed.

rows.label: If treatment is paused
cells: Persistent low blood counts need closer monitoring and can require haematology review. Your team sets the timing of tests before restarting.
Record the stop date. Wait for your team to give you a new dose and restart date.

longitudinal_schedule.note: Your team records the dates and arranges extra tests if your symptoms or results change.

treatment_rationale.summary: In the randomised ATHENA-MONO update, median progression-free survival was 20.2 months with rucaparib and 9.2 months with placebo in the overall trial population (hazard ratio 0.53, 95% CI 0.42–0.69).
treatment_rationale.setting: First-line maintenance after a platinum response
treatment_rationale.limitations: The overall survival estimate remained imprecise (hazard ratio 0.83, 95% CI 0.58–1.17). The trial supports delayed progression and does not establish a survival advantage or an individual duration of benefit.
